His saying, may He be exalted, "Ha Mim": Allah knows best what He intends by it, for these are among the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters, in which one must believe and entrust the meaning to Allah.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, "Ha Mim": Allah knows best what He intends by it, for these are among the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters, in which one must believe and entrust the meaning to Allah.

His saying, "The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise": That is, the revelation of the noble Qur'an is from the presence of Allah, the Mighty in His dominion, the Wise in His creation and management.

His saying, "We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them" of worlds and creatures, "except with truth": That is, only for lofty wisdoms, and not in the way of play and idleness, "and except for a specified term with Him," which is the time of their annihilation and the ending of their existence, to complete the wisdom of their existence.

His saying, exalted is He: "And those who disbelieve turn away from what they were warned of": He informs that those who disbelieve in the Oneness of Allah, His meeting, His signs and His Messenger turn away from what they were warned of, the punishment of Allah that follows from their disbelief and polytheism, paying it no mind; and that is due to the darkness of their souls and the hardness of their hearts.

His saying, exalted is He: "Say: Have you considered what you call upon besides Allah?" That is, the idols and images. "Show me what they have created from the earth": That is, any thing. Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of Muhammad's prophethood (ﷺ) by establishing that the Qur'an is a revelation of Allah sent down upon the Messenger to whom it was revealed, Muhammad (ﷺ).

2- The negation of futility from Allah, may He be exalted, in His creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and in all His actions and sayings.

3- Establishing a factual truth: whoever does not create is not worthy of worship.

4- Clarifying that there is no one more astray in life than one who calls upon someone who never responds to him, such as those who call upon idols, graves and trees under the pretext of tawassul (intercession seeking), istishfa' and tabarruk (seeking blessing).

The noble context continues with the call of the Arabs in general and Quraysh in particular to faith and monotheism. And His words, exalted be He: ﴿He is most knowing of what you plunge into﴾ — that is, Allah, majestic in His majesty, is more knowing than anyone of what you plunge into, rushing into speech, defaming me and the Qur'an, saying of me "a sorcerer" and of the Qur'an "manifest sorcery," saying of me "a fabricator" and of the Qur'an "fabrication," and other such slanders and defects. ﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ — that is, Allah is sufficient as a witness over me and over you concerning what I say and what you say, and He will recompense each for what he has done. ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ — for whoever repents. So repent to Him and He will forgive your disbelief and your plunging into falsehood, and will have mercy upon you, for He, exalted be He, is Forgiving to whoever repents and Merciful to whoever believes and turns back in devotion.

And His words, exalted be He, in verse [9]: ﴿Say: "I am not a novelty among the messengers"﴾ — Allah commands His Messenger to say to those polytheists who plunge into disparaging the Qur'an and the Messenger, during most of their times and most of their gatherings: ﴿I am not a novelty among the messengers﴾ — that is, I am not the first servant to be prophesied and sent, so that I would be an innovation in this matter, to be denied or wondered at on my account; rather, many messengers came before me. And His words: ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner﴾ — that is, I follow only what my Lord reveals to me, in belief, speech, or action, so I never innovate or invent anything Allah has not revealed. ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾ — that is, I am not one who possesses anything for himself or for others, of benefit or harm; I am only a warner of the consequences of disbelief, denial, polytheism, and disobedience. Whoever accepts my warning and refrains from what causes punishment is saved; and whoever rejects my warning, his affair is with my Lord: if He wills, He punishes him, and if He wills, He turns to him in forgiveness, guides him, and shows him mercy.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 46, verse 10–14:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Tell (them): Have you considered?﴾ That is: inform me, what will your condition be?

﴿If it is from Allah﴾: That is, if the Qur'an is from Allah.

﴿And you disbelieve in it﴾: That is, and you denied it, that is, the Qur'an.

﴿And a witness from the Children of Israel testified﴾: That is, and 'Abdullah ibn Salam testified.

﴿To its like, and believed﴾: That is, to the fact that it is from Allah, and he believed.

﴿And you were arrogant﴾: That is, and you were arrogant, so you did not believe. Are you not wrongdoers?

﴿Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it﴾: That is, had what Muhammad brought of the Qur'an and religion been good, the believers would not have preceded us to it.

﴿And since they have not been guided by it﴾: That is, by the Mighty Qur'an.

﴿They will say, "This is an ancient falsehood"﴾: That is, this Qur'an is an ancient falsehood, that is, it is among the lies of the former peoples.

﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and mercy﴾ ... [and this is the book confirming (it)]: That is, the Qur'an confirms the books that came before it.

﴿In Arabic tongue to warn those who have wronged﴾: That is, it is in the Arabic language, so that it may warn with it the wrongdoing polytheists.

﴿And good tidings for the doers of good﴾: It, that is, the Qur'an, is good tidings for the people of excellence in their beliefs, statements and deeds.

﴿Then they remained steadfast﴾: That is, they did not apostatize and continued to perform the obligations and avoid the prohibitions.

﴿No fear will there be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾: That is, in this world, in the barzakh (intermediate state), and on the plains of the Resurrection.

﴿For what they used to do﴾: That is, Allah rewarded them with what He rewarded them, by removing fear and grief from them, for their righteous deeds and their abstention from corrupt deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context remains concerned with guiding the people of the Prophet ﷺ, the Quraysh, who rejected the call and said of its book "clear magic" and of its bearer that he is a fabricator. So Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger: Say, O Muhammad, to those polytheists who said of the Qur'an "clear magic": ﴿Have you considered?﴾ That is, inform me, what will your condition be if the Qur'an is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel, who is 'Abdullah ibn Salam, testifies to its like, that is, to the Torah, that it was sent down from Allah, and it is like the Qur'an. So it is not to be deemed strange that the Qur'an was sent down from Allah, especially since the two books, the Torah and the Qur'an, confirm one another, by both indicating the fundamentals of religion such as monotheism, resurrection, reward with reward and punishment, noble morals, justice, and fulfilling covenants. ﴿So he believed﴾: this witness. ﴿And you were arrogant﴾: that is, and you disbelieved, being arrogant toward faith in the truth. Were you not the worst and most wrongful of people, and deprived of guidance? Indeed Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people, that is, those who wronged themselves through disbelief and sins, so they were deprived of divine guidance.

Allah's saying in verse [11]: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾. This statement may have been made by the Jews of Medina to the believers there, and it may have been made by the polytheists of Mecca and other Arabs, since the intent is an excuse for not accepting Islam on the argument that there is no benefit from it that returns to them in their worldly life and no good they hope for if they enter it; for had it contained the material benefits they hoped for, they would have embraced it and entered it, and the poor and needy would not have preceded them to it.

This is the meaning of what Allah reported about them in His saying ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed﴾, that is, concerning those who said, "Had Islam been good, they would not have preceded us to it," so they believed and we disbelieved. And His saying ﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood"﴾: that is, though their obstinacy became apparent, their rebellion grew great and their arrogance, they were blind and were not guided by the Qur'an, so they will say ﴿This is an ancient falsehood﴾. They have said "the fables of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." The meaning of "ancient falsehood" is a lie invented by someone other than Muhammad and discovered, so he says it. How corrupt this statement is, and how ugly is its speaker!

And His saying ﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, an imam and a mercy﴾: that is, before the Qur'an, whose sending down the polytheists denied, was the Book of Moses, the Torah, which We sent down to him as an imam to be followed, whose followers acting upon its guidance are led to happiness and perfection; and today We sent down the Qur'an as guidance, mercy and good tidings for the doers of good. This is what His saying indicates: ﴿And this is a Book confirming what came before it, in Arabic tongue﴾, that is, We sent it in the Arabic tongue so that Our Messenger to whom it was sent, Muhammad ﷺ, may warn with it those who wronged themselves through polytheism and sins of the punishment of Allah that results from the corruption of souls with the filth of polytheism and sins; and it is good tidings for the doers of good among the believers, who perfected intention and action, of the great success on the Day of Resurrection, which is deliverance from the Fire and entry into Paradise. And His saying ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾: after the Exalted mentioned the falsifiers and their falsehood, He followed this with mention of the doers of good and their deeds, in the manner of warning and encouragement. He informed that those who say "our Lord is Allah," that is, believed and declared their faith and proclaimed it, then remained steadfast upon the path of "there is no god but Allah," worshipping Allah in what He legislated and abandoning the worship of others until they died upon that, these—Allah informs about them that no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve, in this world, in the barzakh, and in the Hereafter. So they are secure in the three lives. He also gave them the good news of Paradise, informing that they are its companions, abiding in it forever, and indicated that that success and good news were the result of their deeds in this world, of faith and righteous action, which is indicated by His saying ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The importance of testimony, that it is a means by which truth is established and falsehood is nullified; therefore the witness must be of good standing ('adala), and 'adala is generally the avoidance of major sins and guarding against minor ones.

5. Glad tidings of Paradise for the Siddiq and his family, since they all believed, all submitted, and died upon that.

*An ukhraja* (أن أخرج): that I should be brought out from the grave alive after my death.

*Wa-qad khalat al-qurun* (وقد خلت القرون): meaning that nations passed before me, and none of them came out of his grave.

*Wa-huma yastaghithani Allah* (وهما يستغيثان الله): meaning they both seek Allah's aid, asking that their son return to faith after his unbelief and denial.

*Ulā'ika alladhina haqqa 'alayhimu al-qawl* (أولئك الذين حق عليهم القول): meaning that the Word of punishment on the Day of Resurrection has become binding upon them.

*Fi umamin qad khalat min qablihim* (في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم): meaning among the nations that passed before them, from both jinn and humankind.

*Wa-li-kulli darajatun mimma 'amilu* (ولكل درجات مما عملوا): meaning that for each of the righteous believers and each of the wicked disbelievers there are degrees according to their deeds: the believers' degrees in Paradise and the disbelievers' degrees in the Fire.

*Adhhabtum tayyibatikum fi hayatikumu al-dunya* (أذهبتم طيباتكم في حياتكم الدنيا): meaning they will be told, "You used up your good things by busying yourselves with the pleasures of this world."

*Wa-istamta'tum biha* (واستمتعتم بها): meaning you enjoyed them in this worldly life.

*Fa-al-yawma tujzawna 'adhab al-hun* (فاليوم تجزون عذاب الهون): meaning your recompense is the punishment of humiliation.

*Bima kuntum tastakbirun fi al-ard* (بما كنتم تستكبرون في الأرض): meaning you were arrogant on earth.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When Allah mentioned the believing man, his righteous deeds and his honourable stances, He here mentioned the disbelieving man, his false deeds and his evil stances. This is by way of calling to Him through both encouragement and warning. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the one who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you threaten me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?"﴾. Allah informs us of the most wicked of people: that atheist who disobeys his parents and denies the Resurrection and recompense. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And for all are degrees according to what they did﴾, means that for each of the righteous believers and the disobedient disbelievers there are degrees according to what they did, of good or evil. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 46, verses 21–25:

Explanation of the words:

"وٱذْكُرْ أخا عادٍ": i.e., the Prophet of Allah Hud (peace be upon him).

"إذ أنذر قومه بالأحقاف": i.e., he warned his people of the punishment of Allah in the valley of al-Ahqaf.

"وقد خلت النذر": i.e., the messengers had passed away.

"من بين يديه ومن خلفه": i.e., from before him and after him, to their nations.

"ألا تعبدوا إلا الله": i.e., warn them that they should not worship anyone but Allah.

"إني أخاف عليكم": i.e., if you worship other than Allah.

"عذاب يوم عظيم": i.e., a terrifying day, because of your associating partners with Allah and your disbelief in my message.

"أجئتنا لتأفكنا عن آلهتنا": i.e., to turn us away from worshipping them.

"فأتنا بما تعدنا": i.e., the punishment for worshipping them.

"إن كنت من الصادقين": i.e., in that it will certainly come to us as you say.

"قال إنما العلم عند الله": i.e., knowledge of the coming of the punishment is not mine; it belongs to Allah alone.

"وأبلغكم ما أرسلت به إليكم": i.e., I am only a messenger who conveys to you what my Lord has sent me with.

"ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون": i.e., you are ignorant of what is good for your own souls and what befits them of happiness and perfection; otherwise, how would you hasten the punishment, demanding it?

"فلما رأوه عارضا": i.e., they saw the punishment as a cloud appearing on the horizon.

"مستقبل أوديتهم": i.e., heading toward their valleys in which were their farms.

"قالوا هذا عارض ممطرنا": i.e., they said, pointing to the cloud, "This is a cloud that will bring us rain."

"بل هو ما استعجلتم به": i.e., it is not the rain-bringing cloud; rather, it is the punishment you demanded hastily.

"ريح تدمر كل شيء": i.e., a violent wind that destroys everything it passes over.

"بأمر ربها": i.e., by the permission of its Lord, exalted is He.

"فأصبحوا لا يرى إلاّ مساكنهم": i.e., He destroyed them entirely, so nothing remained but their dwellings.

"كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين": i.e., such is the recompense We gave to 'Ad, the people of Hud, namely total destruction; We recompense the criminals among all other nations in the same way.

Explanation of the verses' meanings:

The noble context continues on the aim of guiding the people of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Allah the Exalted says, ﴿And mention﴾, i.e., to your people, for lesson and admonition, ﴿the brother of 'Ad﴾, who is Hud (peace be upon him). The brotherhood here is one of lineage, not of religion. Mention him ﴿when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf﴾, when he warned them of the punishment of Allah if they did not repent to Allah and affirm His oneness. Al-Ahqaf is the valley of the people, where their farms and dwellings were, located between Hadramawt, Mahra and Oman in the south of the Arabian Peninsula. His saying ﴿And warners had already passed away before him and after him﴾, i.e., messengers had passed away before him and after him among their nations. That is, Hud was not the first warner, nor was his nation the first nation to be warned of punishment. His saying ﴿that you worship none but Allah﴾, i.e., every messenger warned his nation of the consequence of association and commanded them to worship none but Allah. This is the meaning of "There is no god but Allah," to which Muhammad ﷺ called his nation; it is a command to worship Allah and abandon association. His saying ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, a terrifying, great day, which is the Day of Resurrection. The people's response was what Allah the Exalted related in His saying ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?"﴾, i.e., to turn us away from worshipping our gods, ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with﴾, i.e., the punishment, ﴿if you should be of the truthful﴾ regarding what you threaten and warn us of. Hud (peace be upon him) answered them with what Allah the Exalted related of him in His saying ﴿He said, "Knowledge is only with Allah"﴾, i.e., he said: knowledge of the coming of the punishment and determining its time is not mine; it belongs to Allah, who sends it down. My duty is to warn you of the punishment before it descends upon you, and to convey to you what I was sent with: the command to affirm God's oneness and the prohibition of association and sins. ﴿But I see you to be a people who are ignorant﴾, i.e., of what harms you and benefits you in this world and the Hereafter; otherwise, how would you hasten the punishment and demand it, when you should be seeking mercy and happiness rather than punishment and misery? Allah the Exalted says, ﴿So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys﴾, i.e., when the people of Hud saw the punishment heading toward their valleys in which were their farms and dwellings, ﴿they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾, i.e., this is a cloud appearing in the sky, heading toward our valley to water us. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain﴾, i.e., one that will water our lands, which were afflicted with severe drought.

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿Rather, it is what you were impatient for﴾, i.e., it is not the rain-bearing cloud; rather, it is the punishment you demanded because of your ignorance and lightness of judgment. He clarified it in His saying ﴿a wind containing painful punishment﴾, i.e., carrying within it painful torment, destroying everything it passes over, ﴿by the command of its Lord﴾, i.e., by His permission. It overtook them entirely, and none were saved except Hud and those who believed with him, by a special mercy from Allah. ﴿So they became not seen except their dwellings﴾, i.e., when the observer looked at them, he saw nothing but their dwellings, empty with no one in them. Allah the Exalted says, ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾, i.e., such is the recompense of destruction and annihilation; We recompense the criminals, that is, those who corrupt themselves with association and sins.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of Allah's custom with nations in sending messengers to them.

2- Explanation of the duty of the messengers, which is warning and conveying the message.

3- Explanation of the foolishness and ignorance of nations that demand punishment and hasten it.

4- Explanation that 'Ad were destroyed by the wind al-Dabur, and that our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was aided by the east wind (al-Saba), as in the authentic hadith.

5- Explanation of Allah's custom in destroying criminals, those who persist in association and sins.

Explanation of the words:

﴿Idh kanu yajhadna bi-ayat Allah﴾ (Since they used to deny the signs of Allah): i.e., because they were denying the signs of Allah, which are His clear proofs.

﴿Wa-haqa bihim ma kanu bihi yastahziʾun﴾ (And there descended upon them that which they used to mock): i.e., there descended upon them the punishment that they used to mock.

﴿Wa-laqad ahlakna ma hawlakum min al-qura﴾ (And We had certainly destroyed what is around you of cities): i.e., of the people of the cities, such as ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan.

﴿Wa-sarrafna al-ayat laʿallahum yarjiʿun﴾ (And We directed the signs variously that they might return): i.e., We repeated the proofs, struck the parables, and varied the methods, that they might return to the truth and believe and affirm the Oneness of God.

﴿Bal dallu ʿanhum﴾ (Rather, they vanished from them): i.e., they were absent from them when the punishment descended.

﴿Wa-dhalika ifkuhum wa-ma kanu yaftarun﴾ (That was their falsehood and what they used to fabricate): i.e., their deities' abandonment of them and their failure to support them, but rather their absence from them, was their falsehood and their fabrication that they used to invent.

Explanation of the meanings of the verses:

The context continues on the aim of guiding the Quraysh. When God related to them the story of ʿAd, in which many admonitions and a great lesson were manifest, He said to them: ﴿And We had certainly established them﴾, i.e., the people of ʿAd, We established them in the earth and gave them manifestations of material strength ﴿in that wherein We have established you﴾, you, O assembly of the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿and We made for them hearing and sight and hearts (afʾidah)﴾, i.e., hearts, ﴿but their hearing did not avail them, nor their sight, nor their hearts, of anything of availing, since they were denying the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., His proofs and clear evidences that indicate the obligation of His Oneness, ﴿and there descended upon them﴾, i.e., there came down upon them the punishment with which, when they were warned and admonished, they mocked and derided. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And We had certainly destroyed what is around you of cities﴾, such as ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan.
